[TICK #207, 2026-09-15 23:00 PT] ROOT CAUSE FOR THE 3600 s EXECUTOR DEATHS IS IN launch_queue.py AND IT IS THIS TASK'S. DEGRADED_TRIOS row 0 is ('ornith-1.5:pool','ornith-1.5:pool','ornith-1.5:pool') - all three roles on ONE backend. The table's OWN comment states the defect: 'Removing the second ornith slot at 02:15 left ONE slot, and all-ornith trios then serialise every role of every run through it.' The mitigation written to fix that - seating the qwen3.8:27b span as MANAGER to split the load across two slots - was REMOVED 2026-09-10 09:50 (Paxton: 'all qwen models will forward to ornith1.5', and calling qwen3.8 reloads ~10 GB of VRAM), but ROW 0 WAS LEFT IN PLACE. So the row now carries the serialisation hazard with its mitigation deleted. ornith is a hybrid SSM and Ollama refuses parallel requests on it (n_seq_max=1) - concurrency comes only from multiple instances, and the :11438 deployment was removed from the router 2026-09-10 02:15 for host RAM. COST SO FAR: six tasks / eight runs died at EXACTLY 3600 s on an ornith executor (120, 130, 121 x3, 169, and task 136 twice). DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY RAISING DEGRADED_CAP OR BY SETTING OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL - the table comment forbids both, and DEGRADED_CAP was already lowered 3->2 after ptait01 OOM-killed llama-server twice. BUT READ THIS BEFORE BANNING ALL-ORNITH, BECAUSE THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG: all-ornith IS NOT uniformly fatal. Run 20260916T030730Z_e0802980 (task 107) is bound all-ornith on trio 0 - read from its launcher-recorded roles_bound, not inferred - and it is the fleet's most productive run (round 6/14, PR #108 shipped on powerplatform). The discriminator is CONTENTION FOR THE SINGLE SLOT, not the trio: 107 had the slot to itself from 20:07 PT; every 3600 s death was a run sharing it. SO THE FIX IS A CONCURRENCY INTERLOCK, NOT A BLACKLIST - cap concurrent runs whose executor resolves to ornith-1.5:pool at ONE, and hold the rest, rather than removing row 0 (which in degraded mode would leave the queue with nothing to run at all, the exact failure Paxton's 2026-09-09 22:45 instruction created DEGRADED_TRIOS to prevent). MEASURED THIS TICK: 22:52 launched a SECOND all-ornith run (136) alongside 107 - two runs, one slot, the first time this pairing has existed; ceilings at 23:36 PT (107 r6) and 23:53 PT (136 r1). || *** SECOND MEASURED INSTANCE OF THE DEGRADED-MODE BINDING DEFECT, 2026-09-15 21:05 PT, scheduled tick #197 [7e851a]. Task 136 run 20260916T023708Z_67ca5039 has queue-entry trio="kimi" but roles_bound={manager: ornith-1.5:pool, executor: ornith-1.5:pool, auditor: glm-5.3:cloud} - the launcher bound BOTH local roles to ornith in degraded mode and IGNORED trio=kimi, exactly as task 114 already recorded for run 20260915T101052Z_911af3b6. TWO tasks, two runs, same defect - this is reproducible, not anecdotal. CONSEQUENCE, measured: 136 round-1 cli_executor FAILED at 3600.2s (worker.log) having emitted 12,948,243 chars and produced NET-ZERO CHANGE - it rewrote all three target scripts in infrastructure/scripts/ to content byte-identical to HEAD 5fd2ba8 (fresh mtimes 20:13-20:15 PT, yet git status --porcelain lists none of them). So the cost of this defect is not a slow run, it is a full hour of wall clock per round burned on a model that cannot converge. Whatever retry/terminal logic this task adds MUST honour the queue entry trio, and SHOULD treat a 3600s executor timeout as terminal for the binding rather than retrying the same binding next round. ***

This note (from #207) proposes "cap concurrent runs whose executor resolves to ornith-1.5:pool at ONE". That cap is necessary but NOT sufficient, and this tick measured why. Run 20260916T065253Z_7784478f (task 98) held the single ornith slot with its round-2 EXECUTOR from 00:55:40. Run 20260916T070917Z_0945b502 (task 96) started its round-2 MANAGER at 01:11:13 and was still in it at 01:25:29 - 14+ minutes and counting, against 116 s for that same run's round-1 manager (00:09:17 -> 00:11:13) measured when the slot was free. A manager, not an executor, starved behind an executor. An executor-only interlock would have permitted exactly this pairing, so it must count ANY role that resolves to ornith-1.5:pool toward the cap of one. *** THE CONTROL EXPERIMENT IS IN AND IT EXONERATES THE EXECUTOR PHASE. #227 left two live hypotheses: the executor phase itself is broken, or the ornith backend is. Same harness, same phase, same night. The executor phase is fine; the fault is the ornith slot. *** RUNNING COST, RECOUNTED: this note said six tasks / eight runs dead at exactly 3600 s. Add task 96 round 1 (executor 00:11:13 -> agent.runtime.failed 01:11:13, 3600 s) and task 98 round 1 (duration_ms 3600239, error "Agent timeout", LEDGER line 26038). NOW EIGHT TASKS / TEN RUNS. *** NOT ACTED ON, DELIBERATELY: 96 and 98 bound their trios at launch, so stop-and-requeue onto synthetic is the only way to move them - but the ledger standard for that is a SECOND timeout on the same role, and neither has one yet (96 round 2 has not reached its executor; 98 round-2 executor ceiling is 01:55:40). No rounds granted, no scope cut, nothing stopped. Both hazards this note already forbids - raising DEGRADED_CAP, setting OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL - remain forbidden. *** TICK #229 2026-09-16 01:33 PT - ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED IN THE RUNNING LAUNCHER. THE TWO SYNTHETIC FALLBACKS WERE INERT: they selected an all-Synthetic trio and the rotation loop threw the selection away one block later. launch_queue.py:695 (KEYS SHORT) and :709 (SPAN FULL) both set roles=_trio_syn(_SEQ[0]); line 761 then ran roles=_trio(_SEQ[0]+attempt) UNCONDITIONALLY, overwriting it. So both guards printed their message and changed nothing. This is the SAME bug the `qwen` branch carried and had fixed on 2026-09-10 05:37 (its comment at :750 says so in as many words: 'the first version of this fallback selected QWEN and then the rotation loop overwrote roles with _trio(...) anyway'); the fix was never applied to the two Synthetic fallbacks. MEASURED END TO END, NOT INFERRED: (1) log 01:25 'SPAN FULL (qwen=2 >= 2) -> all-Synthetic trio hivemind-booking-branch-merge'; (2) the very next line probes '[trio 1]', i.e. raw _TRIOS[1], whose executor is ornith-1.5:pool - _trio_syn would have returned one of SYN_ONLY=[2,3,4,5], every one of them ornith-free; (3) the launched run 20260916T082745Z_f470982f has role_configs.executor = ornith-1.5:pool, read from its snapshot. The guard that exists precisely to keep work OFF the contended single-slot local executor put work ON it. THIS IS THE MECHANISM BEHIND THIS NOTE'S OWN 8-TASKS/10-RUNS 3600 s TALLY. FIX APPLIED AND DEPLOYED (not merely edited): a per-task _forced_syn flag set by both fallbacks, and line 762 now reads roles=(_trio_syn if _forced_syn else _trio)(_SEQ[0]+attempt), so rotation still walks several trios but stays inside the all-Synthetic rows once a fallback has fired. 4-line diff, py_compile clean, CRLF preserved (796 CRLF / 1 pre-existing bare LF, backup launch_queue.py.bak-tick229). That remains task 172's work, and it is still needed - the fix only stops the launcher DISCARDING its own avoidance decision; nothing yet counts live ornith roles, so the normal (non-fallback) path can still seat ornith on trios 0 and 1, which is exactly how runs a10da13c and f470982f got ornith executors at 01:25. Both hazards this note forbids - raising DEGRADED_CAP, setting OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL - remain forbidden. *** MEASURED FACT, tick #238 (2026-09-16 03:0x PT), read from the LIVE router, not inferred: the ornith aliases have TWO deployments each, not one. GET /model/info on CT202 127.0.0.1:4000 (master key sourced in-container from /opt/cognizioware-mcp-tools/mcp-tools.env) returns, for each of ornith-1.5:pool, ornith-1.5--256k and ornith-1.5: api_base 192.168.21.110:11438 AND 192.168.21.110:11441, both ollama_chat/ornith-1.5:9b-256k, rpm 20 each. 218 models in the catalog. THIS DOES NOT LICENCE RAISING DEGRADED_CAP OR SETTING OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL - both remain forbidden by this note - and it does not tell you the two ports are two GPUs: they are the same HOST on different ports, and :11438 is recorded elsewhere as the ollama-cloud RELAY while tick #237 measured ornith resident in VRAM on both via /api/ps. Those two readings are UNRECONCILED. What the count DOES settle is the occupancy interlock this note specifies: an interlock that assumes ONE routable ornith slot would be wrong - it must count TWO, or it will hold work that the router could in fact have placed. Related: tick #238 also KILLED the contention hypothesis (three role completions under genuine two-executor overlap), so do not build the interlock to relieve contention that was never demonstrated; build it to stop ornith being seated on trios 0 and 1 at all.

=== MEASURED 2026-09-16 07:55 PT, scheduled overseer tick #277 — THE EXECUTOR TIMEOUT IS BIMODAL, AND THAT KILLS THE 'OVERSIZED SCOPE' READING ===

max_rounds=12), ALL rounds, not a sample:

  COMPLETED:

    round 4  1299 s
    round 8  **76 s**
SIX of nine executor rounds hit the wall; the three that returned returned FAST, one of them in 76 s.
TWO CONCLUSIONS THIS SETTLES:
 (a) THREE-STRIKES DISCRIMINATOR VERDICT: the failure stayed on the SAME role (executor) six times and
     never moved between roles. Per the standing rule that is a BACKEND fault, not scope.
     *** DO NOT CUT TASK 98'S SCOPE. *** It has already been cut and cutting again treats the symptom.
 (b) It is not "slow", it is HUNG. A genuinely overloaded span degrades continuously; it does not return
     in 76 s on round 8 and then consume a full hour on round 9 against the same workspace and the same
     scope. The distribution is bimodal — return in minutes, or never. That is a hang/stall signature
     (no progress, no partial output, exit_code -1, runtime_signals EMPTY), which is this task's subject.
     Note this ALSO does not fit the contention hypothesis that tick #238 already killed.
COST, so the priority is arguable from numbers rather than feel: this single run has spent ~6 h of one of
only TWO launcher slots producing timeouts, while 23 tasks sit HOLD at cap. It has rounds 10-12 left, i.e.
up to ~3 h more at a measured ~2/3 timeout rate.
DELIBERATELY NOT DONE by tick #277: the run was NOT stopped. It is at round 10/12, rounds 2/4/8 produced
real work, and stopping it strands nine rounds to fix nothing — the backend is the fault, not the run.
WHAT WOULD PROVE A FIX: an executor round that fails FAST with a runtime signal instead of burning 3600 s
of wall clock. A retry/terminal-detection change that shortens the wall is worth more here than any
scope edit, because the wall time is the resource being lost.

2026-09-16 17:55 PT - TICK #334 - NEW DEFECT, MEASURED: `synthetic_failing_real_work()`
MIS-ATTRIBUTES AN INFRASTRUCTURE OUTAGE TO SYNTHETIC AND SUPPRESSES THE WHOLE QUEUE.
================================================================================
Symptom: cycles 17:29 and 17:44 both printed `synthetic=DOWN` and held EVERY queued task under
"degraded mode at cap 2". Task 86/99/106, requeued by tick #331 after the CT202 OOM, could not
relaunch for 30 minutes.

Synthetic was NOT down. Measured this tick: keys_ok=3 at 17:44, router /health/liveliness 200 in
0.48s, ZERO `RateLimitError` in the CT202 router log over the last 45 min. What set the flag is the
OTHER half of the gate, `synthetic_failing_real_work(window_s=1800, threshold=2)` (launch_queue.py
~L580): it counts runs with status `failed`, `updated_at` inside 1800s, and `:synthetic` anywhere in
`role_configs`. The three runs killed by the 17:16:06 CT202 OOM all stamped `failed` at 17:28:5x -
`cd77d50b` (106) and `52a5447e` (86) carry `:synthetic` roles, so n=2 >= threshold 2. The counter
cannot tell "Synthetic is refusing work" from "the router OOMed and 502'd every in-flight run".

Consequence, and why this matters more than the 30 minutes: an infra outage AMPLIFIES ITSELF. The
outage kills N synthetic runs; their death then gates the queue for a further 30 minutes; the
requeued work sits idle exactly when capacity has just been freed. Tick #331 restored the router in
13 minutes and the fleet still launched nothing for the next two cycles.

Self-clears at 17:58:58 PT (1800s after the last casualty stamp), so tick #334 did NOT hot-patch:
a patch needs a launcher restart and the window was shorter than the restart's own risk.

THE FIX BELONGS TO THIS TASK: `synthetic_failing_real_work()` must EXCLUDE runs whose failure cause
is transport, not provider. The failures are distinguishable in the run's own log - the OOM
casualties all died on `API Error: 502 status code (no body)` (47 hits each, read in context by
tick #331), which is the ROUTER refusing, not Synthetic. A provider-side failure shows
`RateLimitError` / 429 from the upstream. Suggested shape: read each candidate's final error and
count it only when it is a 429/RateLimit, or at minimum skip the window entirely when the router
was observed down inside it.

CORRECTS TICK #332, which recorded "the 17:29 `keys_ok=0 synthetic=DOWN` was an OUTAGE ARTIFACT,
not capacity - the watcher's 17:15 probe died TimeoutExpired mid-outage; 17:35 reads ok: 3". The
`keys_ok=0` half of that is right. The `synthetic=DOWN` half is not, and the difference is load-
bearing: keys_ok recovered at 17:35 while the DOWN flag persisted through 17:44 under a DIFFERENT
mechanism. Blast radius: one row (#332), ~15 minutes, no action taken on the wrong belief - #333
did not act on the flag either.

[TICK #337, 2026-09-16 18:15 PT] LOCAL-LANE CAP UNDER-COUNTS: `_local_exec` READS THE EXECUTOR ONLY.
launch_queue.py:221 `_local_exec(roles)` returns True only when roles['executor']['model'] lacks ':synthetic'
and ':cloud'. The SPAN-FULL guard (~line 722) is `elif qw>=LOCAL_CAP and _local_exec(roles)`, so a run that seats
the local lane in its MANAGER or AUDITOR role costs the accounting NOTHING while still consuming a real slot.
MEASURED, not theorised: run 20260916T173404Z_ab8d54f9 (task 107) has role_configs manager=ornith-1.5:pool AND
executor=ornith-1.5:pool. It counts as ONE toward LOCAL_CAP=2 while occupying up to TWO of the lane's slots
(OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2, rpm=20). So the guard admitted task 100 onto a lane that was already full, and 100's
executor then timed out at the full 1800s budget in rounds 1 and 3 (r3 emitting exactly 16 MiB), gating the run at
18:11:52. Full evidence in 743-100's note.
THE FIX IS ONE PREDICATE, not a redesign: count local occupancy across ALL THREE roles, i.e. make the per-run cost
`sum(1 for c in roles.values() if local(c['model']))` rather than a bool on the executor. Note LOCAL_CAP=2 is
documented as '= OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL' (line 343), which is a count of SLOTS - so comparing it against a count of
RUNS was already a unit mismatch; this makes that explicit.
SEPARATE FROM the `synthetic_failing_real_work` finding recorded here by tick #334 - different predicate, different
failure mode. Both are launcher accounting bugs; neither is hot-patchable without a restart (a file edit is not a
deploy - the running launcher is pid 63324, started 16:39:35).


MEASURED 2026-09-16 20:33:56 (tick #356) - A NEW CRASH CLASS, AND IT KILLED THE LAUNCHER OUTRIGHT. `launch_queue.py` died with FileNotFoundError at line 631 (`json.load(open(f))`) on `C:/tmp/queue/_t355_75700773.json`: an overseer SCRATCH file written into the queue directory and deleted while the cycle was iterating its own glob snapshot. The loop had NO per-file guard, so one vanished file terminated the whole process and the queue stopped draining until the next tick happened to read the log. Tick #356 fixed the cause in place (glob skips `_*` basenames; each load wrapped in try/except FileNotFoundError/OSError/ValueError logging `SKIP unreadable queue file`) and restarted it as PID 52400. WHAT THIS TASK STILL OWES: (a) the launcher has no supervisor - nothing restarts it when it dies, and the death was silent on every operator surface; a crash should self-restart or at minimum be visible; (b) the top-level cycle should be wrapped so ANY unexpected exception logs and continues to the next cycle rather than exiting; (c) the 'is the launcher alive' check must be by PROCESS + log growth, since a stale log alone reads as healthy.
